Joel 1 · The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

precepts.text: The Most High sets His prophet over the nations to root out, pull down, and destroy, which is why Ezekiel had to prophesy Tyrus's total ruin to her face.
precepts.point: His horses shall cover her with dust and tread down her streets; he shall slay her people, spoil her riches, prey on her merchandise, break her walls, destroy her pleasant houses, and lay her stones, timber, and dust in the midst of the water. He will cause the noise of her songs to cease and make her like the top of a rock, a place to spread nets, built no more.
precepts.why:
The Most High told Jeremiah, “See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.” That is what a prophet is set over the nations to do, and that is why Ezekiel had to prophesy Tyrus's total ruin to her face.

Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, “a king of kings, from the north”, comes with horses, chariots, horsemen and much people. Babylon serves as the Most High's sword against the nations that thought our downfall was their gain. He slays her daughters in the field, makes a fort and casts a mount against her, sets engines of war against her walls and breaks down her towers with his axes. The dust of his horses covers her, her walls shake at the noise of the horsemen and the wheels and the chariots, and he treads down all her streets.

They spoil her riches, prey on her merchandise, break down her walls, destroy her pleasant houses, and lay her stones, timber and dust “in the midst of the water”. The noise of her songs ceases, and she is made “like the top of a rock”, “a place to spread nets upon”, built no more. Rooted out, pulled down, destroyed, thrown down: “for I the Lord have spoken it”.

precepts.text: Every shipmaster and sailor stands afar off and cries at the smoke of the great city's burning, casting dust on their heads and lamenting how in one hour so great riches came to nought.
precepts.point: They shall take up a lamentation, asking how she is destroyed, that renowned city inhabited of seafaring men which was strong in the sea and caused terror on all who haunted it. This parallels the fall of the great seafaring city that reflects Esau's nation today.
precepts.why:
At the fall of Tyrus “all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and lay away their robes”, clothe themselves with trembling and sit upon the ground astonished, taking up a lamentation: “How art thou destroyed, that wast inhabited of seafaring men, the renowned city, which wast strong in the sea”. Revelation has the same scene at the fall of the great city. “For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off, And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city!”

They cast dust on their heads, weeping and wailing: “Alas, alas, that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate.” Seafaring men, renowned in the sea, made rich by her, lamenting her in one hour.

That is the parallel. The fall of Tyrus, the great seafaring city, reflects the fall of Esau's nation today. The isles tremble in the day of her fall, and the isles in the sea are troubled at her departure.

precepts.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, the cry of astonishment over the downfall of the proud, renowned power, matched again in the judgment of Tyrus.
precepts.point: They shall take up a lamentation, asking how she is destroyed, that renowned city inhabited of seafaring men which was strong in the sea and caused terror on all who haunted it. This parallels the fall of the great seafaring city that reflects Esau's nation today.
precepts.why:
The princes of the sea cry, “How art thou destroyed”, astonished that the renowned city which caused terror on all that haunt it could fall. Isaiah records that same cry over Lucifer: “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!”

It is the cry of astonishment over the downfall of the proud, renowned power, the one who weakened the nations, and it is matched again in the judgment of Tyrus. She who was strong in the sea and made the isles shake is cut down, and the princes lay away their robes and tremble at every moment.

That is what waits for the great seafaring city that reflects Esau's nation today: the same fall, the same astonishment.

precepts.text: The Most High brings Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings, from the north; Babylon is called the destroyer of the Gentiles because the Most High used them as a sword against Tyrus and the other heathen nations, not just against Israel.
precepts.point: A nation has come up upon his land, strong and without number, whose teeth are the teeth of a lion and the cheek teeth of a great lion. This is how we know the time period; if you are familiar with the book of Daniel, the nation represented as the lion is Babylon.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

precepts.why:
“For thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I will bring upon Tyrus Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings, from the north, with horses, and with chariots, and with horsemen, and companies, and much people.” The lion from the north is Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings, and the Most High is the one who brings him.

Babylon is called the destroyer of the Gentiles because the Most High used them as a sword against Tyrus and the other heathen nations, not just against Israel. That is the nation strong and without number that came up upon the land, the lion of Daniel, Babylon.

points: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word comes because Tyrus said against Jerusalem, Aha, she that was the gate of the peoples is broken and turned to me, so I shall be replenished now she is laid waste. Tyrus saw our loss of Jerusalem as their come-up and profit.

Therefore the Most High is against Tyrus and will cause many nations to come up against her like the sea casting up its waves; they shall destroy her walls, break her towers, scrape her dust, and make her like the top of a rock, a place for spreading nets, and her daughters in the field shall be slain.

The Most High will bring Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings from the north, with horses, chariots, and horsemen, to slay her daughters, build a fort, cast a mount, and set engines of war against her walls and towers. Babylon serves as His sword against the nations that thought our downfall was their gain.

His horses shall cover her with dust and tread down her streets; he shall slay her people, spoil her riches, prey on her merchandise, break her walls, destroy her pleasant houses, and lay her stones, timber, and dust in the midst of the water. He will cause the noise of her songs to cease and make her like the top of a rock, a place to spread nets, built no more.

At the sound of Tyrus's fall the isles shall shake and the wounded cry, and all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, lay away their robes, put off their broidered garments, and clothe themselves with trembling, sitting on the ground astonished.

They shall take up a lamentation, asking how she is destroyed, that renowned city inhabited of seafaring men which was strong in the sea and caused terror on all who haunted it. This parallels the fall of the great seafaring city that reflects Esau's nation today.

The Most High will make Tyrus a desolate city like cities uninhabited, bring up the deep upon her, and cover her with great waters, bringing her down with them that descend into the pit to the low parts of the earth. He is putting the whole island and civilization under water forever.

He will make her a terror, and she shall be no more; though she be sought for, she shall never be found again, because she said Aha when we suffered judgment. The city once beautiful and top-notch is wiped out because of how it mocked the judgment of the Most High.
